title: Why North European Steel Coil Rose €10 to €770 a Tonne as Energy Costs Shut Mills and Import Quotas Run Out
dek: North European steel coil prices rose €10 to €770 a tonne as energy costs shut mills and import quotas ran out, according to kalkine.co.uk.
summary: According to a kalkine.co.uk headline, North European steel coil rose €10 to €770 a tonne. The headline attributes the rise to energy costs shutting mills and import quotas running out. No excerpt was provided, so the product grade, timeframe and which mills were affected are not stated.
keyFacts: North European steel coil rose €10 a tonne
Energy costs have shut mills, per the headline
Import quotas have run out, per the headline
whyItMatters: The combination of supply curtailed by energy costs and exhausted import quotas could tighten European flat-steel availability and support further price firmness.
implications: European coil buyers may face reduced import alternatives until quotas reset, while exporters to Europe, including Indian mills, should watch quota timing closely.
